One count is neither exhaustive write inventory nor proof of isolation. In particular, calling it merely logs would wrongly use excluded outer captures to explain an included entry.

    58	**D. Less work: no observed reduction in computation.** Every invocation logs all requested units, with no `Skipping ... because it already exists` marker. Across all 32 unit executions, independently compared these per-unit log records against a-1: four map-write messages, two identical ASA computation/skipped/out counts, ranked ligand generation 1–50, and result copy-out. Status `no` answers whether evidence shows less computation, not whether every conceivable reuse mechanism has been excluded.

Local comparison does not remove unknown shared-state effects, but rules out simple a-1-only timing anomaly. Status: `yes`.

   101	Serial a occupies only about 7.3 of 26 logical CPUs on average, about 28–29% host busy. Two concurrent invocations reach about 12.3 effective cores/47.5% busy; four reach about 19/73–75%. Despite hundreds of live threads, average active CPU use remains much smaller: thread count is not CPU saturation. Eight MPI ranks per docking invocation (`U:27`; native log `L/a-1:39`) fit observed serial occupancy; serial native/assembly/scoring phases can reduce average use further. Parallel independent units fill idle capacity.
   102	
   103	Memory remains plentiful: minimum across arms 215027160 KiB, about 205.1 GiB and 92.7% of total. Invocation max RSS values range 2387564–2542560 KiB (about 2.28–2.42 GiB); wait4 max RSS is not sum of simultaneous process memory. These data supply no memory-capacity-pressure explanation. Memory bandwidth/cache misses and separate I/O wait durations were not measured, so smaller overlap/cache contributions cannot be quantified or ruled out. Busy fraction is host-wide and can include unrelated work; effective cores is measured command CPU time divided by arm wall (`P:395–425`; `S:131`). Agreement between their trends strengthens occupancy explanation.
   104	
   105	Four-unit separate invocation mean exceeds baseline-own serial mean by 179.068143 s, 16.75046%. This includes repeated startup, imports, scoring and other invocation overhead; it is not pure startup measurement. Such costs count against published gain, not a source of cheaper later computation. Concurrent CPU totals exceed a totals while wall drops, consistent with more work per second across idle CPUs. Width-four per-unit invocation walls (336–470 s) also exceed corresponding b walls (273–389 s), so throughput gain is from overlap, with contention, rather than each unit becoming intrinsically faster. Exact division among MPI efficiency, serial phases, OS scheduling, and memory/I/O overlap remains unmeasured. Best-supported status: `idle_cpu_in_serial_mode`.
   106	
   107	Validation performed: parsed saved JSON; checked sample/reference path sets; recomputed means, factors, repeat deltas and nearby-arm ratios; scanned every invocation log and compared per-unit map/ASA/rank markers; checked run11/run10 harness/fix bytes and source identifiers. No numerical workload or probe executed. Remaining principal uncertainty is identity/use of counted shared entry; complete result equivalence and causal attribution beyond listed PDBs/resource trends are not established.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run_units.sh - the measured baseline restricted to original prepared input records.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_units.sh <system_id:kind>...   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). Command paths are relative;
     6	# absolute PATH entries and TMPDIR are inherited from run_command.sh (see REPORT.md).
     7	# PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     8	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     9	#
    10	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    11	# data/selection.json; requested holo/apo jobs only, n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    12	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    13	# `pinder_eval` (50 decoys per selected job). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    14	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    15	#
    16	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    17	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    18	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    19	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    20	set -Eeuo pipefail
    21	[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: at least one system_id:kind is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    22	
    23	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    24	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    25	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    26	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    27	MPI_NP=8
    28	FORCE=false
    29	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    30	METHOD=frodock
    31	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    32	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    33	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    34	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    35	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    36	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    37	CUDA_SEL=""
    38	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    39	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    40	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    41	  fi
    42	done
    43	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    44	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    45	fi
    46	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    47	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    48	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    49	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    50	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    51	
    52	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    53	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    54	RESULTS="out/results"
    55	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    56	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    57	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then
    58	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    59	  mv "$RUN_DIR"/*.log "$RUN_DIR"/*.yaml "$RUN_DIR"/*.json "$RUN_DIR"/*.tar.gz "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/" 2>/dev/null || true
    60	fi
    61	# Preserve decoys and scoring output from earlier invocations as well as logs.
    62	if [ -d "$RESULTS" ]; then
    63	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    64	  mv "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/results"
    65	fi
    66	exec > >(tee "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log") 2>&1
    67	mkdir -p out/tmp
    68	export TMPDIR="$PWD/out/tmp"
    69	
    70	for f in "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" data/selection.json data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv; do
    71	  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "ERROR: $f missing; run harness/setup.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
    72	done
    73	for b in frodockgrid_mpi_gcc frodock_mpi_gcc frodockcluster_gcc frodockview_gcc soap.bin; do
    74	  [ -e "baseline-published/frodock/bin/$b" ] || { echo "ERROR: FroDock $b missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    75	done
    76	
    77	# fresh results tree: force=false would otherwise skip jobs whose decoys already exist

    85	
    86	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ printed configuration (validated)
    87	"$VPY" - "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv" data/selection.json \
    88	    "$METHOD" "$N_SOLUTIONS" "$MPI_NP" "$FORCE" "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS" "$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT" <<'PY'
    89	import json, os, sys, yaml
    90	import pandas as pd
    91	from pinder.core import get_index
    92	cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])); jobs = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[2]); sel = json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
    93	idx = get_index()
    94	s = idx[idx["pinder_s"].astype(bool)]
    95	apo = s[s["apo_R"].astype(bool) & s["apo_L"].astype(bool)]
    96	ids = sorted(set(apo["id"]))[: sel["n"]]
    97	print(f"PINDER_S_SYSTEM_COUNT={s['id'].nunique()}")
    98	print(f"PINDER_S_APO_PAIRED_COUNT={apo['id'].nunique()}")
    99	print("SELECTED_IDS=" + json.dumps(ids))
   100	errs = []
   101	if sys.argv[4:] != ["frodock", "50", "8", "false", "8", "0"]: errs.append("actual command parameters differ from fixed configuration")
   102	if os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES") != "": errs.append("CPU baseline must expose zero GPUs")
   103	if os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR") != "data" or os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE") != "2024-02": errs.append("dataset environment differs from fixed configuration")
   104	if ids != sel["ids"]: errs.append("selection from index differs from data/selection.json")
   105	if sel["n"] != 8 or len(ids) != 8: errs.append("representative scale must contain exactly 8 systems")
   106	if cfg != {"n_solutions": 50, "mpi_np": 8, "force": False}: errs.append(f"config {cfg} is not the published representative config")

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run_command.sh - the exact measured baseline command and its complete environment.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_command.sh   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). All paths are relative to that
     6	# working directory. PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     7	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     8	#
     9	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    10	# data/selection.json, holo and apo pairings (16 docking jobs), n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    11	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    12	# `pinder_eval` (800 decoys). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    13	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    14	#
    15	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    16	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    17	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    18	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    19	set -Eeuo pipefail
    20	
    21	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    22	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    23	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    24	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    25	MPI_NP=8
    26	FORCE=false
    27	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    28	METHOD=frodock
    29	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    30	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    31	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    32	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    33	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    34	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    35	CUDA_SEL=""
    36	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    37	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    38	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    39	  fi
    40	done
    41	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    42	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    43	fi
    44	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    45	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    46	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    47	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    48	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    49	
    50	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    51	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    52	RESULTS="out/results"
    53	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    54	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    55	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then
    56	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    57	  mv "$RUN_DIR"/*.log "$RUN_DIR"/*.yaml "$RUN_DIR"/*.json "$RUN_DIR"/*.tar.gz "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/" 2>/dev/null || true
    58	fi
    59	# Preserve decoys and scoring output from earlier invocations as well as logs.
    60	if [ -d "$RESULTS" ]; then
    61	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    62	  mv "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/results"
    63	fi
    64	exec > >(tee "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log") 2>&1
    65	mkdir -p out/tmp
    66	export TMPDIR="$PWD/out/tmp"
    67	
    68	for f in "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" data/selection.json data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv; do
    69	  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "ERROR: $f missing; run harness/setup.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	done
    71	for b in frodockgrid_mpi_gcc frodock_mpi_gcc frodockcluster_gcc frodockview_gcc soap.bin; do
    72	  [ -e "baseline-published/frodock/bin/$b" ] || { echo "ERROR: FroDock $b missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    73	done
    74	
    75	# fresh results tree: force=false would otherwise skip jobs whose decoys already exist
    76	mkdir -p "$RESULTS"
    77	cat > "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" <<EOF
    78	n_solutions: $N_SOLUTIONS
    79	mpi_np: $MPI_NP
    80	force: $FORCE
    81	EOF
    82	cp data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv"   # predict reads <results_dir>/frodock_setup.csv
    83	
    84	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ printed configuration (validated)
    85	"$VPY" - "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv" data/selection.json \
    86	    "$METHOD" "$N_SOLUTIONS" "$MPI_NP" "$FORCE" "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS" "$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT" <<'PY'
    87	import json, os, sys, yaml
    88	import pandas as pd
    89	from pinder.core import get_index
    90	cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])); jobs = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[2]); sel = json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
    91	idx = get_index()
    92	s = idx[idx["pinder_s"].astype(bool)]
    93	apo = s[s["apo_R"].astype(bool) & s["apo_L"].astype(bool)]
    94	ids = sorted(set(apo["id"]))[: sel["n"]]
    95	print(f"PINDER_S_SYSTEM_COUNT={s['id'].nunique()}")
    96	print(f"PINDER_S_APO_PAIRED_COUNT={apo['id'].nunique()}")
    97	print("SELECTED_IDS=" + json.dumps(ids))
    98	errs = []
    99	if sys.argv[4:] != ["frodock", "50", "8", "false", "8", "0"]: errs.append("actual command parameters differ from fixed configuration")
   100	if os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES") != "": errs.append("CPU baseline must expose zero GPUs")
   101	if os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR") != "data" or os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE") != "2024-02": errs.append("dataset environment differs from fixed configuration")
   102	if ids != sel["ids"]: errs.append("selection from index differs from data/selection.json")
   103	if sel["n"] != 8 or len(ids) != 8: errs.append("representative scale must contain exactly 8 systems")
   104	if cfg != {"n_solutions": 50, "mpi_np": 8, "force": False}: errs.append(f"config {cfg} is not the published representative config")
   105	if sorted(set(jobs["id"])) != sorted(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv ids differ from selection")
   106	if sorted(set(jobs["kind"])) != ["apo", "holo"] or len(jobs) != 2 * len(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv is not holo+apo for every id")
   107	if set(zip(jobs["id"], jobs["kind"])) != {(pid, kind) for pid in ids for kind in ("holo", "apo")}: errs.append("frodock_setup.csv lacks an expected id/pairing")
   108	print(f"CONFIG method=frodock subset=pinder-s pairs=holo,apo n_jobs={len(jobs)} n_solutions={cfg.get('n_solutions')} "
   109	      f"mpi_np={cfg.get('mpi_np')} force={cfg.get('force')} CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='{os.environ.get('CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES')}' "
   110	      f"host_nproc={os.cpu_count()} PINDER_BASE_DIR={os.environ.get('PINDER_BASE_DIR')}")
   111	if errs:
   112	    sys.exit("ERROR: " + "; ".join(errs))
   113	PY
   114	echo "GPU_COUNT=$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT CUDA_SELECTION=$CUDA_SEL MPIRUN=$(command -v mpirun) FRODOCK_BIN=$(dirname "$(command -v frodock_mpi_gcc)")"
   115	echo "PINDER_VERSION=$("$VPY" -c 'import importlib.metadata as m;print(m.version("pinder"))')"
   116	
   117	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ published docking command
   118	set +e
   119	"$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" predict --method "$METHOD" --data_dir data/frodock \
   120	    --results_dir "$RESULTS" --subset pinder-s --pairs all --config "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml"
   121	PRED_RC=$?
   122	set -e
   123	echo "PREDICT_EXIT=$PRED_RC"
   124	[ "$PRED_RC" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: pinder_methods predict exited $PRED_RC" >&2; exit "$PRED_RC"; }
   125	
   126	# FroDock 3.12 writes small molecules as HETATM with a blank chain. The published adapter
   127	# concatenates receptor + transformed ligand without restoring that label. Restore only blank
   128	# ligand HETATM labels, retaining every atom, coordinate, rank and all other PDB bytes. Identify the
   129	# ligand suffix by its existing L-labelled atoms. FroDock's output atom count need not equal the
   130	# input reader's count (e.g. alternate locations); validate emitted records, not that equality.
   131	# Keep original decoys and a change manifest beside the saved command output.
   132	"$VPY" - "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR" <<'PY'
   133	import csv, json, sys, tarfile
   134	from pathlib import Path
   135	import biotite.structure.io as strucio
   136	
   137	results, run_dir = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
   138	changes = []
   139	with tarfile.open(run_dir / "raw_decoys.tar.gz", "w:gz") as originals:
   140	    for job in csv.DictReader(open(results / "frodock_setup.csv")):
   141	        directory = results / "frodock" / job["id"] / (job["kind"] + "_decoys")
   142	        for model in sorted(directory.glob("model_*.pdb")):
   143	            lines = model.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
   144	            atom_lines = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith(("ATOM  ", "HETATM"))]
   145	            if not atom_lines or lines[atom_lines[0]][21:22] != "R":
   146	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: missing receptor prefix")
   147	            restored = []
   148	            in_ligand = False
   149	            for line_index in atom_lines:
   150	                line = lines[line_index]
   151	                chain = line[21:22]
   152	                if chain == "L":
   153	                    in_ligand = True
   154	                    continue
   155	                if chain == "R" and not in_ligand:
   156	                    continue
   157	                if not in_ligand or chain != " " or not line.startswith("HETATM"):
   158	                    raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: unexpected chain on PDB line {line_index + 1}")
   159	                restored.append(line_index + 1)
   160	            if not in_ligand:
   161	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: missing labelled ligand atoms")
   162	            if restored:
   163	                originals.add(model, arcname=model.relative_to(results))
   164	                for line_number in restored:
   165	                    line = lines[line_number - 1]
   166	                    lines[line_number - 1] = line[:21] + "L" + line[22:]
   167	                model.write_text("".join(lines))
   168	                changes.append({"file": str(model), "line_numbers": restored, "chain": "L"})
   169	            chains = set(strucio.load_structure(str(model)).chain_id)
   170	            if chains != {"R", "L"}:
   171	                raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {model}: invalid chains {chains}")
   172	json.dump(changes, open(run_dir / "chain_labels_restored.json", "w"), indent=2)
   173	print(f"CHAIN_LABELS_RESTORED models={len(changes)} atoms={sum(len(c['line_numbers']) for c in changes)}")
   174	PY
   175	
   176	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ published scoring command
   177	# pinder_eval asks for interactive confirmation for every subset/pairing with systems not run here;
   178	# answer yes so the published missing-system penalty is applied (no --allow_missing).
   179	set +e +o pipefail
   180	yes y | "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" --eval_dir "$RESULTS" --method_name "$METHOD" --max_workers "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS"
   181	EVAL_RC=${PIPESTATUS[1]}
   182	set -e -o pipefail
   183	echo "EVAL_EXIT=$EVAL_RC"
   184	[ "$EVAL_RC" -eq 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: pinder_eval exited $EVAL_RC" >&2; exit "$EVAL_RC"; }
   185	exit 0

   206	        n_solutions : int

   214	    complex_kind = str(complex_config["kind"])
   215	    complex_receptor = Path(complex_config["receptor"])

    10	def process_starmap(
    11	    func: Callable[..., Any],
    12	    args: Iterable[Iterable[Any]],
    13	    parallel: bool = True,
    14	    max_workers: int | None = None,
    15	) -> list[Any]:
    16	    if parallel:

    20	        outputs = []
    21	        for args_i in tqdm(args):

    23	    return outputs

    26	def process_map(
    27	    func: Callable[..., Any],
    28	    args: Iterable[Iterable[Any]],
    29	    parallel: bool = True,
    30	    max_workers: int | None = None,
    31	) -> list[Any]:
    32	    if parallel:
    33	        with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Pool(processes=max_workers) as pool:
    34	            outputs = pool.map(func, args)
    35	    else:
    36	        outputs = []
    37	        for args_i in tqdm(args):
    38	            outputs.append(func(args_i))
    39	    return outputs

     2	
     3	Use PINDER-S as the primary benchmark: https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder
     4	
     5	It contains 250 protein–protein test complexes, including 93 with paired unbound structures. Prioritise those 93 cases for realistic docking evaluation. Use the published AAV–AAVR structures 6IHB, 6JCQ and 6JCS as a separate, biologically motivated challenge.
     6	
     7	These represent AAV2–PKD2, AAV1–PKD2 and AAV5–PKD1 interactions. The AAV challenge should initially evaluate redocking from separated components. Do not treat these as independently determined unbound structures.
     8	
     9	Investigate the following questions:
    10	- Can existing docking methods recover known protein–protein interfaces from the benchmark inputs?
    11	- What limits the number of independent candidate poses that can be evaluated or searched concurrently?
    12	- Could restructuring the search exploit massively parallel GPU hardware rather than merely distributing independent runs?
    13	- Does additional search improve the probability of recovering experimentally observed interfaces within a fixed time or compute budget?
    14	
    15	Evaluate scientific correctness using DockQ, interface RMSD and native-contact recovery. DockQ ≥ 0.23 defines an acceptable-quality prediction under the standard benchmark convention.     18

    22

     4	#
     5	# On Unix we run a server process which keeps track of unlinked
     6	# resources. The server ignores SIGINT and SIGTERM and reads from a
     7	# pipe.  Every other process of the program has a copy of the writable
     8	# end of the pipe, so we get EOF when all other processes have exited.

   124	  - `b-1`: four invocations of one unit each, one after another in sample order;

   126	  - `c4-1`: all four started together;
   127	  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
